docs.title: Foreword
docs.text: Welcome to the official Bot House documentation! This guide is designed to help you quickly set up, manage, and build custom automated bots for both Discord and Telegram.

docs.title: What is Bot House?
docs.text: Bot House is a powerful, visual, and scriptable bot creation platform. It allows users to build feature-rich bots across multiple messaging platforms using simple, intuitive functions—no complex backend setup or coding background required.

docs.title: Supported Platforms
docs.text:
• Discord: Create custom commands, auto-moderation, embeds, buttons, and event triggers.
  • Telegram: Build custom command flows, interactive menus, inline queries, and multi-user chat bots.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Cross-Platform Support: Deploy and manage bots on Discord and Telegram from a single platform.
  • Simple Functional Syntax: Use readable, tag-based function signatures like $title[...], $description[...], and $sendMessage[...].
  • Rich Embeds & Formatting: Fully customize message appearance with titles, thumbnails, footer banners, and action components.
  • Built-in Hosting: Manage your bots seamlessly with active hosting and built-in runtime tools.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
Here is a simple example showing how a basic command response works in Bot House:

$title[Welcome to Bot House!]
$description[Your bot is ready to serve both Discord and Telegram channels.]
$thumbnail[https://example.com/bot-house-logo.png]
$sendMessage[Hello world!]

docs.title: Navigation & Getting Started
docs.text:
• Quick Start Guide: Learn how to connect your bot tokens and write your first command.
  • Functions Reference: Explore the complete list of supported scripting functions.
  • API Reference: Access the public API endpoints and JSON data schema.

docs.title: API Documentation
docs.text: Our documentation offers a JSON API endpoint that exposes the list of supported functions, their arguments, descriptions, and metadata. This endpoint can be used to build autocomplete features, syntax highlighters, or custom docs viewers.

docs.title: Functions List Endpoint
docs.text:
Retrieve a full list of available scripting functions and their parameter signatures.

  • URL: /api/discord/cmd.json
  • Method: GET
  • Response Format: application/json

docs.title: Response Structure
docs.text:
The endpoint returns an array of function objects structured as follows:

Field Type Description tag String Full function signature (e.g., $footer[text;footer icon]). description String A concise summary of what the function does. arguments Array List of parameter objects expected by the function.

docs.title: Argument Object Structure
docs.text:
Each object inside the arguments array contains:

Field Type Description name String Name of the parameter. description String Explanation of what to pass for this parameter. type String Expected data type (String, URL, Number, etc.). required Boolean Whether the argument is mandatory. empty Boolean Whether an empty value can be passed.

docs.title: Example Response
docs.text:
[
  {
    "tag": "$footer[text;footer icon]",
    "description": "Sets the footer text and optional icon for an embed.",
    "arguments": [
      {
        "name": "text",
        "description": "The footer text.",
        "type": "String",
        "required": true,
        "empty": false
      },
      {
        "name": "footer icon",
        "description": "Direct URL to a footer icon image.",
        "type": "URL",
        "required": false,
        "empty": true
      }
    ]
  }
]

docs.title: Welcome to BHScript!
docs.text: Welcome to the official documentation for the Bot House! This language allows you to build powerful Discord bot responses using simple, readable function syntax.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Simple Syntax: Functional syntax built around square brackets like $function[arguments].
  • Rich Embed Support: Easily format titles, descriptions, images, and footers for Discord messages.
  • Message Sending: Control where and what messages are sent with minimal code.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
$title[Hello World!]
$description[This is my very first Discord script!]
$footer[Powered by Discord Scripting;https://example.com/icon.png]
$sendMessage[Check out this cool response!]

Get started by checking out the Quick Start Guide or dive straight into the Embed Functions Overview.

docs.title: Embed Functions
docs.text: Embed functions allow you to customize the layout and visual presentation of rich Discord embeds.

docs.title: $title
docs.text: Sets the title of the current embed.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: $title[text]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description text String Yes The header title for the embed.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: $title[Server Rules]

docs.title: $description
docs.text: Sets the main description text for the embed.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: $description[text]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description text String Yes The main content body of the embed.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: $description[Please be respectful to everyone in the server.]

docs.title: $footer
docs.text: Adds a footer banner at the bottom of the embed, with an optional icon.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: $footer[text;footer icon]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description text String Yes Text shown at the bottom of the embed. footer icon URL No Direct URL to an image for the footer icon.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: $footer[Page 1 of 5;https://example.com/footer-icon.png]

docs.title: $thumbnail
docs.text: Displays a small image in the top-right corner of the embed.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: $thumbnail[image url]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description image url URL Yes A valid image URL (http:// or https://).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: $thumbnail[https://example.com/logo.png]

docs.title: $image
docs.text: Displays a large, full-width image inside the main body of the embed.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: $image[image url]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description image url URL Yes A valid image URL (http:// or https://).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: $image[https://example.com/banner.png]

docs.title: Messaging Functions
docs.text: Functions used to dispatch and control messages within a channel.

docs.title: $sendMessage
docs.text: Sends a text message along with any created embed objects to the current channel.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: $sendMessage[text]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description text String Yes Plain text content to send alongside the embed response.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
$title[Announcement]
$description[Maintenance starting in 10 minutes!]
$sendMessage[Attention @everyone!]

docs.title: Functions Overview
docs.text:
Below is the current list of supported functions in the scripting language.

Function Category Description $title[text] Embed Sets the title of the embed. $description[text] Embed Sets the main body description of the embed. $footer[text;icon url] Embed Sets the footer text and optional footer icon. $thumbnail[image url] Embed Sets the small thumbnail image on the top right. $image[image url] Embed Sets the main large image inside the embed. $sendMessage[text] Messaging Sends a message/embed response to the channel.

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text: This guide will help you understand how functions work in this scripting language.

docs.title: Basic Concepts
docs.text: Functions always start with a dollar sign ($), followed by the function name, and enclose their parameters inside square brackets ([...]).

docs.title: Syntax Format
docs.text:
$functionName[arg1;arg2;...]
  • Arguments: Separated by a semicolon ; when a function accepts multiple inputs.
  • Order: Functions are evaluated in order from top to bottom.

docs.title: Building Your First Embed
docs.text:
To send an embed response, combine embed structure functions with a message trigger:

$title[Welcome Server Member!]
$description[We are glad to have you here.]
$thumbnail[https://example.com/welcome-avatar.png]
$sendMessage[Welcome!]

docs.title: User Functions
docs.text: Functions for retrieving information about Discord users, including IDs, usernames, and display names.

docs.title: $authorID
docs.text: Returns the unique Discord snowflake ID of the user who triggered the command.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: $authorID

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This function takes no parameters.

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text: $sendMessage[Your user ID is $authorID!]

docs.title: $username
docs.text: Retrieves the account username of a specified user or the command author.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: $username[userID]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description userID Number No The target user's snowflake ID. Defaults to the command author if left blank.

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text:
Retrieve author's username:


$sendMessage[Hello, $username!]

Retrieve specific user's username:


$sendMessage[User details for: $username[123456789012345678]]

docs.title: $displayName
docs.text: Retrieves the global display name or server nickname for a user.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: $displayName[userID]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description userID Number No The target user's snowflake ID. Defaults to the command author if left blank.

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text:
Greeting with display name:


$sendMessage[Welcome back, $displayName!]

In an Embed:


$title[$displayName's Profile]
$description[User ID: $authorID]
